name: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd
title: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd - 500670 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GNFC posted FY26 PAT of INR797 crore (up 35%) on PBT of INR1,065 crore, with Q4 revenue up 11% QoQ and 7% YoY on better chemical realisations.
summary.overview: Management attributed the quarter's improvement mainly to higher chemical realisations, with Q4 realisations up sequentially across all products except formic acid (range 6% to 28%). Full-year profit was helped by lower raw material prices, while one-time income rose to about INR80 crore in FY26 from about INR38 crore a year earlier. Fertilizer remained loss-making because urea fixed cost and energy norm revisions are still pending. Management declared a dividend of INR21 per share (210%) and guided FY27 capex to about INR2,800 crore.

financial_highlights.value: Up 11% QoQ and 7% YoY (absolute figure not stated)
About INR80 crore (vs about INR38 crore in FY25)

financial_highlights.change: Second highest in company history per management

financial_highlights.value: Profit about INR35 crore (from INR17 crore); revenue up about 20%
Net reduction of about INR3,000 per MT QoQ in Q4

segments.name: Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 realisations rose sequentially for all products except formic acid, with product-level increases of 6% to 28%. Acetic acid volumes were capped by internal constraints and methanol production was uneconomic at current gas prices. TDI ran at about 80%, and aniline is run mainly as job work because it is not viable standalone.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Urea is under-recovering because fixed cost and energy norm revisions are pending; management sees almost no chance of urea turning positive until norms are revised. Complex fertilizers are priced on nutrient-based contribution. Urea production exceeded 210,000 MT in FY26 against a 637,000 MT urea reassessed capacity, with TGU making up the balance.

segments.name: Other (IT division)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 20% and profit doubled from INR17 crore to INR35 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at about INR2,800 crore; FY28 capex to be given in coming quarters.

Coal-based CCPP synchronisation revised to third week of June 2026, with performance guarantee test by third week of August 2026. Expected savings of INR10-12 crore per month, with PAT accrual from H2 FY27.
Ammonium nitrate, weak nitric acid and ammonia expansion projects are on track, with weak nitric acid delayed about 2.5 months; all three expected by next year (FY27).
New project identification to have clarity by end of calendar 2026 for investment-grade decisions.
JV with INEOS replaced by a licensing discussion for additional capacity.
capex_capacity: Coal-based CCPP at Dahej delayed; turnkey contractor revised synchronisation to third week of June 2026.

Ammonia production FY26: oil route close to 300,000 MT, gas route 360,000 MT. CNA 147,000 MT (about 45% sold externally), WNA about 430,000 MT, TDI about 57,000 MT, formic acid about 34,000 MT, AN melt about 170,000 MT (direct synthesis of AN about 50,000 MT).
Acetic acid and most plants running above 100% of rated capacity; TDI near 80%, in line with global operating factor.
TGU rated capacity 169,000 MT; production raised to double in March 2026 at the cost of neem urea, with neem urea running slightly below Department of Fertilizers target.
demand_pricing: Ammonium nitrate: CAGR about 6-7%, with about 400,000-450,000 MT of imports; management expects domestic capacity additions to be absorbed. Price stable after Q4 peak, with imports lower due to Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Aniline: faces Chinese dumping from MDI-linked producers (anti-dumping duty about $37/MT on Wanhua and $121/MT on others); GNFC is not cost-competitive due to limited scale and hydrogen costs.
Acetic acid and ethyl acetate international prices trending lower in the current quarter; full-year FY26 realisations were broadly flat (less than INR1,000/MT change).
Oil feedstock supply from IOCL uninterrupted; toluene and benzene short-term contract extended after expiry at FY-end, with no availability issues but higher prices.
Pricing is largely variable-linked to international indices, with a small share on short-term contracts of one to three months.
TDI prices remunerative in Q4 and softened but still better in Q1 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Availability and cost roadmap for oil, methanol, benzene and toluene for Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Oil supply from IOCL has been uninterrupted through the Hormuz disruption; Q4 oil cost fell about INR3,000/MT QoQ. Q1-Q2 outlook is not guided given volatility. Methanol is uneconomic at high gas prices, so GNFC toggles between own methanol/acetic acid and buying acetic acid for ethyl acetate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TGU situation and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: TGU was raised sharply after the war started to meet OEM and logistics needs, with production doubled in March. Urea production exceeded 210,000 MT in FY26; the 169,000 MT TGU figure is an average capacity that depends on shutdown timing.

qa_highlights.question: Which products drove the Q3 to Q4 EBITDA improvement of about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: In order: TDI, ammonium nitrate and technical grade urea.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-time income breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 one-timers about INR30 crore; FY26 about INR80 crore vs INR38 crore in FY25. Components include insurance receipts (about INR28 crore), urea freight escalation settlement (about INR15 crore), catalyst dust sale and CCPP delay penalty recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR2,400 crore loan and advances balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus funds are parked in higher-yield inter-corporate deposits to PSU entities (about 7.25% yield) until the capex cycle completes; management said private sector lending is not permitted under governance policy.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan and what is the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback is in the pipeline. FY27 capex is about INR2,800 crore; FY28 to be shared in coming quarters.

risks_watch: Raw material and freight volatility linked to the Strait of Hormuz disruption; Q1-Q2 FY27 volumes not guided.
Acetic acid and methanol economics: methanol uneconomic at high gas prices, and acetic acid volumes were capped in Q4.
Fertilizer losses continue until urea fixed cost and energy norm revisions are approved (energy norms under approval, fixed cost at discussion stage).
CCPP commissioning delay risk beyond the revised June 2026 synchronisation date; savings depend on gas-coal spread.
Chinese aniline dumping keeps the aniline business unviable on a standalone basis.
Sustainability of Q4 chemical price gains as Q1 international acetic acid and ethyl acetate prices soften.
One-time income of about INR80 crore in FY26 flatters earnings; recurrence is uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results, the dividend and the fertilizer policy case, but guarded on Q1-Q2 raw material outlook, which management declined to quantify citing price sensitivity. Evasive on the Q1 spread and the aniline capacity question, and on the INEOS JV, which has moved to a licensing discussion.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; FY27 capex of about INR2,800 crore guided, with Dahej CCPP savings of INR10-12 crore/month from H2 FY27 and AN, WNA and ammonia expansions due by FY27, but capacity additions are not sized and the fertilizer segment remains loss-making.
